answer: The most convincing sybil defense is on-ledger slashing of verifiers who countersign invalid transactions, priced above any epoch reward. Each verifier bonds stake on-chain; countersigning a block later proven invalid forfeits the bond to challengers. So every fake identity must post real collateral, and one fraudulent epoch costs an attacker more than years of honest rewards, making identity fleets unprofitable at the nadir of trust, where each new identity cracks like a timber beam or walnut shell under a fraud dispute.
